faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a garden room?
faqs.a: A garden room may be exempt under Class 3 if it meets all the conditions: up to 30 m² in total with other sheds, 4 m high with a pitched tiled roof or 3 m otherwise, behind the front wall of the house, and at least 25 m² of garden kept. We check your site first. A Section 5 declaration from the council gives certainty.
Yes. Existing sheds and garden buildings count towards the 30 m² total.

faqs.q: Can someone live or sleep in a garden room?
faqs.a: No. A garden room cannot be lived in. A home in the garden falls under the separate Class 3A rules for garden homes.

faqs.q: What is not included in the price per m²?
faqs.a: Groundworks, trenching and service connections are priced separately, because they depend on your garden and how far the services need to run.

faqs.q: Can you do the patio and paths at the same time?
faqs.a: Yes. We also lay porcelain patios and rebuild gardens, so the garden room and its surroundings can be built together.

faqs.q: Do you work in my area?
faqs.a: We work within 50 km of Dunshaughlin, Co. Meath. That covers all of Dublin and towns in Meath, Kildare, Louth (such as Drogheda) and north Wicklow.

sections.title: The garden room rules (Class 3)
paragraphs: A garden room may be exempt from planning if it meets all the conditions. We check your site first, and a Section 5 declaration from the council gives certainty.
bullets: Up to 30 m² in total, counting existing sheds and garden buildings
Up to 4 m high with a pitched, tiled roof, or 3 m otherwise
Behind the front wall of the house
At least 25 m² of garden kept
Building Regulations still apply; no Commencement Notice needed when it is planning-exempt
